text: Piglets are caught by one rear leg and then held in various ways for injection, castration, or teeth clipping — they are light but move vigorously. For fattening pigs, farmers often try to inject without restraint, which is a common cause of incorrectly placed injections; procedures needing a still animal require a pig catcher — even a simple strong rope with a slipknot works, since pulling back hard on the upper jaw once caught stops the pig moving further. A pig catcher can also be used on sows, though sows kept in individual crates can usually be handled for most procedures without needing to be caught at all.
